# .github/AGENTS.md — CI-failure runbook

Read this file when a check fails, not before.

You are editing an enforcement instrument. Read the vendored `ENFORCEMENT.md` before this lands.

## Reproduce locally

```bash
pnpm check:ci         # everything reusable-checks.yml runs: check:static plus every package's tests
pnpm check:static     # the static-checks job alone (format, lint, typecheck, type tests, attw, build)
pnpm --filter <pkg> test --shard=<i>/<n>   # one shard of a test job
```

## Standing facts

- **Each CI lane owns its turbo cache key prefix** (`turbo-<os>-<lane>-<sha>`). actions/cache keys are immutable: lanes sharing a key race, and the faster lane's partial save silently drops the slower lane's entries.
- **Test jobs are planned from recorded timings.** The `plan` job reads the newest `test-timings-<profile>` artifact from main, or from any branch when main has none, and balances packages over the fewest free `ubuntu-latest` jobs whose loads fit 5 minutes (`scripts/tools/test-timings.ts`). Each job builds first, then runs its packages' tests one at a time (`turbo run test --concurrency=1`), so its wall time is the sum it was planned from and each recorded duration is uncontended. The test run keeps the builds in its graph, never `--only`, so each test key carries every dependency's build hash; the builds are cache hits after the build step. A package over 5 minutes runs as vitest shards. The `timings` job records every measured package into this run's `test-timings-<profile>` artifact, so the next run of the same profile re-packs automatically.
- **The reusable workflows are shared with other repositories.** Consumers call them pinned by commit SHA; their contract is [Calling the reusable workflows](#calling-the-reusable-workflows). Everything specific to this repository is in the callers' inputs (`ci.yml`, `mutation.yml`, `commitlint.yml`, `nix.yml`) and in `.github/actions/checks-lane`, this repository's lane hook. To change this repository's steps, edit that action; to change the shape, edit the workflow and keep its inputs backward compatible for pinned callers.
- **A lane picks its conformance profile.** A pull request runs `reusable-checks.yml` with `profile: local`; the merge queue and pushes to main run the default `per-change`; `release.yml` gates at `per-change`. Every lane runs every test file of every package: no lane leaves a test out by its name or location (`CONST-T12`). `local` runs 25 seeds and one preemption, `per-change` keeps what each check asks for. A local run measures different durations than a per-change one, so timing records are keyed by profile (`test-timings-local` / `test-timings-per-change`) and each lane plans from its own measurements.
- **Mutation jobs are planned from the mutants Stryker plans, never on a pull request.** `mutation.yml` triggers on `workflow_dispatch` only and calls `reusable-mutation.yml`, whose `guard` job refuses a pull request before anything installs. Its `plan` job installs the workspace and judges every package with a `mutation` or `mutation:*` script (`scripts/tools/test-timings.ts plan --task mutation`): a Node probe loads the config Stryker would discover and the package's own `@systemfsoftware/stryker-config`, with the job's environment and once per shape a package can take, `STRYKER_SHARD` empty (run whole) and `1/1` (a shard), then again under every `<index>/<count>` once sizing splits a package, and the plan fails before any mutation run with one `::error title=<reason>` annotation per refusal: `mutation-script` (any mutation script but `"mutation": "stryker run"`), `no-workflow-file`, `missing-mutation-script` (a workspace package outside the plan, the root excepted, that holds a file of the shared mutated set as Node's glob expands it), `hidden-workflow-file` (any package holding a file under a hidden path that the shared patterns would match: Node's glob skips it, Stryker's matcher mutates it), `shared-test-file` (the installed `@systemfsoftware/stryker-config`'s shared set holds a test file: upgrade it), and, naming every shape that gave them, `config-unloadable`, `own-mutate-targets`, `non-workflow-target`, `test-file-target` or `shard-partition` (the config's own `!<file>` negations, each naming one shared file verbatim, leave a file of the shared set to no shard, or to more than one, whether the package runs whole or split); a negation that names no shared file verbatim, such as a glob, makes the set the config's own (`own-mutate-targets`); `own-ignore-patterns` (an ignore pattern beyond the shared ones as they stood before the config ran), `ignored-workflow-file` (a shared file under a directory a kept shared ignore pattern, `node_modules` or `*.tsbuildinfo` names, which Stryker's crawl drops), `scoped-mutation` (any `since`) or `own-output-paths` (a Stryker output path, every one of which the crawl ignores, set to a value other than the shared one). It predicts each admitted package as the mutants `stryker plan --full` counts times its seconds per mutant (its own recorded `seconds / mutants`, else the record's slowest rate, else the `unknown-mutant-seconds` input) and packs the packages into free `ubuntu-latest` jobs whose loads fit 15 minutes. A package over 15 minutes splits into shards: `STRYKER_SHARD=<k>/<n>` slices `sharedConfig.mutate`, the shared `workflowMutate` glob, giving each file of the shared set to one shard as Node's glob expands it; a file Stryker's matcher reaches that the expansion missed falls to every shard, and the report job refuses that overlap. The shard count comes from predicted seconds and `--max-jobs`, never from the file count, and a file is never divided, so a package with fewer workflow files than shards leaves some shards with none: each still installs, builds and runs the package's tests once in Stryker's dry run, then finishes with no mutants. `scripts/tools/mutation-job.ts run` runs a job's packages one at a time, each capped at 30 minutes and all within a 60-minute job budget that stays under the runner timeout, and records each duration as it finishes. A capped or failed run records only a lower bound: it can raise a package's duration, so the next plan splits it further, but never lower it, so a run that crashes in its first second cannot pack every package into one job; a package the budget no longer covers is skipped and fails the job. The timings job records each package's planned mutant count beside its duration, so the next plan has a rate. `mutation-job.ts report` folds a package's shard parts into one package report, refusing two shards that mutated the same file and a staged report that is not a complete Stryker report; a shard that stopped before writing its report contributes the verdicts its stream recorded (a mutant line that does not decode fails the merge) and leaves its package incomplete. It merges every package into `mutation-merged/mutation.json`, keyed by repo-relative path under the strictest thresholds any package declares, and `mutation-merged/summary.md`, a row per planned package graded by its own thresholds. A Stryker `break` exit fails no job: it shows only as a `[FAIL]` row. A failed merge keeps the per-job parts (one-day retention) for its reproduce command; a passed one deletes them. Stryker's incremental files travel between runs in one shared `stryker-incremental-*` cache; turbo does not cache mutation.
- **The merge queue is enabled in the `main` ruleset only after this shape is on main.** Every workflow that reports a required check needs the `merge_group` trigger first — `ci.yml` carries it, so the gate reports on the queue ref. Enable the queue with strict up-to-date policy off; strict would need a queue whose required checks already run on `merge_group`.
- **Never re-trigger a release by hand.** `scripts/tools/plan-release.ts` derives the phase from repository state, so a killed release leaves untagged versions the next push re-plans. Tagging and GitHub Releases are idempotent — a version whose `<pkg>@vX.Y.Z` git tag already exists is skipped (`scripts/tools/cycle.ts`, `scripts/tools/tag-released-packages.ts`).
- **There is no registry.** These packages are distributed as this repo's Nix flake outputs consumed from a git ref (pinned by `flake.lock` rev + narHash, bwrap-sandboxed), not published to npm. The release path writes a git tag and a GitHub Release per unreleased version — no npm token, no OIDC, no trusted publisher to configure.

## Calling the reusable workflows

Five workflows are callable from any repository: `reusable-checks.yml`, `reusable-mutation.yml`, `reusable-commitlint.yml`, `reusable-nix.yml` and `conflict-check.yml`. Call them pinned by commit SHA (`uses: systemfsoftware/systemfsoftware/.github/workflows/<file>@<sha>`). Every input is optional except `conflict-check`'s two; a caller writes no composite action of its own.

**Where tools and actions come from.** A reusable reaches this repository's actions through `$/.github/actions/<name>`, which resolves to the workflow's own commit, never the caller's `./`. Its Deno tools (`test-timings`, `mutation-job`, `classify-diff`, `sfs-deps`) come from `$/.github/actions/sfs-tools`, which sparse-checks out `scripts/` at `job.workflow_repository`@`job.workflow_sha`. `$/` needs runner 2.336.0 or newer, so a self-hosted fleet must run at least that. A non-root `working-directory` checks out only that directory (except `reusable-nix.yml`, whose evaluator needs the whole tree's objects).

**Consumer prerequisites.** A pnpm workspace with a committed lockfile and a `packageManager` field. Checks: `turbo`, a `test` script per tested package, and a `build` task where one exists. Mutation: every mutated package has a `src/**/*.workflow.ts` file, a `"mutation": "stryker run"` script and no `mutation:*` variant, and a `stryker.config.*` that spreads `sharedConfig` from `@systemfsoftware/stryker-config` and sets no `mutate`; the plan job runs `pnpm exec stryker plan --full` in each such package, so Stryker must load there after an install with no build. The report job installs nothing, since `mutation-job report` merges every package's parts into the `mutation-report-<run number>` artifact (one `mutation.json` in mutation-testing-report-schema, keyed by repo-relative path, and a `summary.md`). Commitlint: `@commitlint/cli` and a commitlint config in the workspace root. Nix: a flake whose `packages.<system>` and `checks.<system>` are derivations.

**`.sfs-deps` tarballs (checks, mutation, commitlint).** A consumer installs systemfsoftware packages as `file:.sfs-deps/<name>-<version>.tgz` entries in `pnpm-lock.yaml`, with `.sfs-deps/` gitignored, and a flake installable in `working-directory` whose output is a directory holding exactly those `.tgz` files (`sfs-deps-installable`, default `.#sfs-deps`; `.github/consumer-fixture/flake.nix` is the pattern). Each call's `sfs-deps` job keys the tarballs on the `.sfs-deps/` paths and integrities the lockfile records (`sfs-deps-v1-<sha256>`). A warm key restores in every installing job with no Nix; a cold one installs Nix only in that job, builds the installable, checks every named tarball against its recorded integrity and saves only then. Every job that installs restores the key before the hook-or-built-in routing or its install step, so a lane hook's own install finds `.sfs-deps/` in place, and checks each restored tarball against the lockfile's integrity before anything installs it (`sfs-deps-mismatch` on a difference). A lockfile that names no `.sfs-deps/` tarball gets an empty key and no other step.

**Event policy.** On a pull request, checks and nix run only what the diff can affect: a diff inside the docs set (`docs/**`, root `*.md`, `**/AGENTS.md`, `**/CLAUDE.md`, or `docs-globs`) skips build, test and nix; the plan still runs, after the classifier and without a turbo dry run, and only lanes with a `docs-run` run. The built-in `docs` phase installs, so on a docs-only diff the classifier reads the lockfile and skips the `sfs-deps` producer only when it read the lockfile and found no `.sfs-deps/` tarball; otherwise the producer runs, on the base branch's key, since a docs-only diff leaves the lockfile unchanged. Any other event, any path outside the set, or a diff that cannot be read runs everything. The test planner skips a package whose turbo hash a remote cache or a passed run already holds, and nix builds only outputs whose `drvPath` differs from the base commit's (one that fails to evaluate there builds). Mutation runs on push and `workflow_dispatch` only: its `guard` job fails a `pull_request`, `pull_request_target` or `merge_group` event with `mutation-on-pull-request` before anything installs. Commitlint runs on pull requests only and skips Dependabot.

**Permissions the caller grants.** Checks: `contents: read`, `actions: read`. Mutation: `contents: read`, `actions: write` (the plan reads the record, the report deletes per-job artifacts). Commitlint, nix and conflict-check: `contents: read`. Checks takes the `turbo-api` and `turbo-token` secrets for a remote Turbo cache.

**The lane hook (checks only).** A caller that has `.github/actions/checks-lane/action.yml` at the root of its checkout gets it run once per phase (`plan`, a lane's id, `test`, `test-after`, `timings`, `gate`, `docs`) with inputs `lane`, `job` and `profile`; the workflow output `lane-source` is `hook`. Without one, or under a non-root `working-directory`, every phase runs `$/.github/actions/builtin-lane` and `lane-source` is `built-in`; the non-root case says so in the summary with `hook-not-visible-working-directory`. In built-in mode a `timings` of `test-timings` means this workflow's own planner, and `dry-run` defaults to `<pnpm> exec turbo run test --dry=json` on pull requests.

**On failure.** Each failing job writes one reason code, the local reproduce command and the next action to its step summary, annotates with them, and uploads its captured logs as `failure-log-<job>-<attempt>`. The codes are a closed set (`$/.github/actions/failure-summary`): `merge-conflict`, `classify-failed`, `install-failed`, `tools-ref-missing` (sfs-tools got no workflow repository or commit, or could not fetch the tools at that commit), `plan-failed`, `hook-failed`, `lane-failed`, `build-failed`, `test-failed`, `timings-failed`, `gate-failed`, `commit-message-invalid`, `nix-eval-failed`, `nix-build-failed`, `outputs-differ-across-systems`, `compare-artifact-missing`, `mutation-on-pull-request`, `mutation-failed`, `mutation-merge-failed`, `sfs-deps-lockfile-invalid` (the lockfile is unreadable or names one tarball with two integrities), `sfs-deps-build-failed`, `sfs-deps-mismatch` (in the `sfs-deps` job, the installable lacks a named tarball or builds other bytes than the lockfile records; in an installing job, the cache entry restored under the key holds other bytes than the lockfile records), `sfs-deps-missing` (an installing job found no cache entry under the `sfs-deps` job's key, or the cache service refused the restore), and `unclassified` for a failure none of them names.

**This repository dogfoods them.** `ci.yml`, `mutation.yml`, `commitlint.yml` and `nix.yml` are callers, and `consumer-fixture.yml` calls `reusable-checks.yml`, `reusable-commitlint.yml`, `reusable-nix.yml` and the `mutation-event-guard` action on `.github/consumer-fixture/`, a workspace with its own lockfile, no hook and no composite, exactly as an outside repository would. It does not call `reusable-mutation.yml`: the fixture's package holds no workflow file, so it carries no mutation script, and the mutation reusable is exercised only by this repository's own dispatched runs.

### `reusable-checks.yml`

Outputs `lane-source` and `test-jobs` (the planned test jobs as JSON, each with its `packages`; `[]` when every package was skipped); secrets `turbo-api`, `turbo-token`. Inputs stay backward compatible for pinned callers: add, never rename or remove.

| Input                  | Default             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `working-directory`    | `.`                 | The pnpm workspace root, relative to the repository root. A non-root value checks out only that directory and always runs the built-in lanes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `profile`              | `per-change`        | Passed to the checks-lane action unchanged; systemfsoftware's conformance profile (`local` or `per-change`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `record`               | `test-timings`      | Name of the timing record artifact the plan reads and the timings job writes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `timings`              | `test-timings`      | Command that runs the test-timings planner (the flake's `test-timings`, or a deno invocation of the script). With the built-in lanes, `test-timings` is this workflow's own planner                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `runs-on`              | `["ubuntu-latest"]` | JSON label list for the plan, timings and gate jobs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `test-runs-on`         | empty               | JSON label list for the test jobs and any lint lane that names none; empty means `runs-on`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `lanes`                | `[]`                | JSON list of lint lanes: {"id", "name", "timeout-minutes", "run"?, "docs-run"?, "fetch-depth"?, "runs-on"?}; `run` is a command after the lane's action. On a docs-only pull request a lane with `docs-run` runs that command after the `docs` phase instead, and a lane without one is skipped                                                                                                                                                      |
| `target`               | `300`               | Planner --target, seconds of predicted work per job                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `max-jobs`             | `12`                | Planner --max-jobs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `max-seconds`          | `1800`              | Planner --max-seconds; keep it at or under the test job's timeout-minutes in seconds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `timeout-minutes`      | `30`                | Each test job's timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `plan-timeout-minutes` | `5`                 | The plan and timings jobs' timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `gate-name`            | `the gate`          | Name of the job that passes only when every other job passed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `gate-lane`            | `false`             | Check out and run the checks-lane action's `gate` phase after the gate's own check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `gate-timeout-minutes` | `2`                 | The gate job's timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `node-options`         | empty               | NODE_OPTIONS for the test jobs (a lint lane sets its own `node-options`); GitHub refuses it from $GITHUB_ENV                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `pnpm`                 | `pnpm`              | How the test steps invoke pnpm                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `test-flags`           | empty               | Extra flags on the packed jobs' `turbo run test`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `shard-flags`          | empty               | Extra flags on a shard job's vitest run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `persist-credentials`  | `true`              | actions/checkout persist-credentials                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `fetch-tags`           | `false`             | actions/checkout fetch-tags                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `dry-run`              | empty               | Command printing turbo's `--dry=json` for the test task without `--only` (e.g. `pnpm dlx turbo@2 run test --dry=json`), so each hash covers the task's dependencies as the test jobs' own keys do; the plan skips a package whose task is a remote cache hit, or which last passed whole on the same dry-run hash. Empty plans every package, except that the built-in lanes default it to `<pnpm> exec turbo run test --dry=json` on a pull request |
| `docs-globs`           | empty               | Newline- or comma-separated globs that replace the docs set (`docs/**`, root `*.md`, `**/AGENTS.md`, `**/CLAUDE.md`). A pull request that changes only docs skips the test and timings jobs and runs only lanes with a `docs-run`; the plan still runs                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `turbo-team`           | empty               | Remote Turbo cache team; empty leaves the remote cache off                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `sfs-deps-installable` | `.#sfs-deps`        | The flake installable that builds the lockfile's `.sfs-deps/` tarballs; see [`.sfs-deps` tarballs](#calling-the-reusable-workflows)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Failure runbook

| Failure                     | Root cause                                                      | Remedy                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `api:check` fails           | Public API surface changed in a package with a committed golden | `pnpm --filter <pkg> api:update` and commit `etc/*.api.md`                                            |
| Git step exits 128          | Dirty workspace cascading from a prior step                     | Inspect the first failing step, not the git step                                                      |
| Log download gives HTTP 403 | The GitHub API refuses log download without push access         | Open `https://github.com/systemfsoftware/systemfsoftware/actions/runs/<run_id>` and read the step log |
